what_it_does: Point cloud neural networks (which process 3D spatial data from cameras and sensors) are computationally expensive and run poorly on mobile and edge devices due to irregular data access patterns and heavy memory bandwidth demands. This paper proposes Point-CIM, an accelerator that moves computation into the memory chips themselves rather than fetching data back and forth. The design exploits sparsity—the fact that many numbers in the computation are zero and can be skipped—using a technique called zero-bit-skipping. It also uses a novel data reorganization strategy called Voxel-Morton-sorted Partitioning to improve how efficiently the computation breaks down, along with bit-level quantization (using fewer bits per number) to compress the data without needing extra hardware.
